inputs.caption:
Global Metadata: Bright upbeat anime game music in a cute Q-style chiptune-pop register. 156 BPM in C major, cheerful, bouncy and toy-like. Emotional arc: a sparkling inviting intro, a confident bouncy main theme, a softer middle section that lifts a fourth for contrast, then back to the main theme, a playful breakdown, and a final run through the theme before a clean short outro. This is a FULL-LENGTH looping game track of roughly ninety seconds, so it needs many distinct sections rather than a single short idea. Listening scenario: the background music of a colourful cartoon arena game for kids and grown-ups, played on repeat. Production profile: clean modern chiptune and anime-pop hybrid, crisp and bright, punchy but never harsh, wide stereo sparkle, no distortion, no lo-fi grit.

Vocal Details: Fully instrumental. No vocals, no choir, no vocal chops, no humming, no words of any kind - every section is played by instruments only.

Arrangement: Square-wave chiptune lead, bright glockenspiel doubling the melody an octave above, bouncy rounded synth bass, plucked marimba and kalimba arpeggios, tight electronic drum kit with a snappy snare and crisp closed hi-hats, taiko-style tom fills at the section changes, hand claps on the main theme, shimmering bell accents. Intro: glockenspiel and marimba arpeggio alone, then a four-beat drum pick-up. Main theme: square lead states the melody over the full band with hand claps on beats two and four. Second pass: same melody with the kalimba answering in the gaps. Middle section: the bass drops to a simple pulse and the tune passes to the marimba. Breakdown: drums and lead drop out, leaving arpeggios and a rising build. Final theme: melody returns an octave higher with bell accents and a taiko fill. Outro: everything drops away on the last bar leaving the glockenspiel arpeggio ringing on its own, so the loop point lands cleanly.
